divergences.description: The SSE wire format differs from what the plan describes. Token frames are parsed from a `text` field, not `delta`. `StreamDone` carries only `assistantMessageId`, with no `content` or `createdAt`. Instead of replacing the content with the server's authoritative final text (T008/T022), the message is finalized from the locally accumulated tokens.
The failed-message state shows the 'Falha ao gerar resposta' text above the timestamp, and the timestamp is still shown. The spec (FR-004) and T017 say the failure text replaces the timestamp.
A `_reconcileSilentFailure` step that is not in the plan was added. After a failure with empty content, it calls `listMessages` again and replaces the failed bubble with the persisted server answer.
Global Dio timeouts (connect, send and receive) were added in the service locator. This changes network behavior for every endpoint and is not in the plan.
The drawer gains an unplanned account header: an initials avatar plus a display name built from the email in the JWT, via the new `SecureTokenStorage.readAccountEmail`. This is outside RF04 scope.
A new design token, `sizeAvatarMenu`, was added. The plan says zero new tokens are needed.
When a next page of sessions loads, its sessions are appended to the list without removing duplicates. T039 requires the append to happen 'without duplicates'.

divergences.description: The SSE wire format the code uses is not the one the plan specifies. The plan (T008/T012/T022) says token frames are parsed from `decoded['delta']`, that StreamDone carries `content`/`createdAt`, and that the bloc replaces the message with the server's authoritative final text. The code reads the token from `decoded['text']`, StreamDone carries only `assistantMessageId`, and the bloc finalizes the message from tokens it accumulated locally. Code comments cite the backend's actual zod contract as the reason.
FR-004 and T017 say the 'Falha ao gerar resposta' note replaces the timestamp. In the code the failed bubble shows the note and the timestamp, one above the other.

An unplanned account header was added to the drawer: an initials avatar plus a display name built from the account email. To get the email, the code adds a new `SecureTokenStorage.readAccountEmail()` that decodes the JWT payload. It also adds a new design token, `sizeAvatarMenu`, although the plan says zero new tokens.
The shared Dio instance now has global connect, send and receive timeouts. This is not in the plan, and it changes network behavior for every endpoint in the app.

An unplanned `_reconcileSilentFailure` step was added. When a turn fails with empty content, the bloc calls `listMessages` again and, if the server has a completed answer, swaps it in for the failed bubble. No task covers this.
The spec's Key Entities say a generic placeholder title is shown when a session has an empty title. The drawer renders `session.title` directly, with no fallback.
New widgets hardcode visual values (fontSize 12, padding 10/12, cursor width 2), even though Principle IV/RNF08 require zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.

divergences.description: The SSE event shapes differ from the plan. The plan (T008/T012/T022) has `token` carry `decoded['delta']`, and has `StreamDone` carry `content` and `createdAt`, with the server's final text replacing the locally built content. The implementation reads `token.text` instead. `StreamDone` carries only `assistantMessageId`, and the message is finalized from the locally accumulated tokens. The code says this matches the backend's real wire format (contracts/zod/chat.ts).
The plan (FR-004, US2, T017, T030) puts the 'Falha ao gerar resposta' text in place of the timestamp. The implementation shows the failure text and still shows the timestamp below it.

A best-effort reconciliation step was added that is not in the plan. After a failure with empty content, `_reconcileSilentFailure` calls `listMessages` again and may replace the failed bubble with a completed answer from the server.
Global Dio timeouts were added to the shared Dio instance used by every endpoint (connect/send 15s, receive 30s). The plan does not mention this.

The side menu gained an account header (avatar with initials and a display name) that the plan does not include. The name and initials come from the JWT email via a new `SecureTokenStorage.readAccountEmail`.
A new design token, `sizeAvatarMenu`, was added. The plan states zero new color/spacing/radius tokens for this unit.
A new domain helper, `ChatSessionTimestampFormatter`, was added. It is not among the 5 planned domain entities/helpers, and it sets its own relative-date format for the side menu.
The defensive fallback for an empty session title is missing. The spec calls for a generic placeholder title when a session's title is empty; the drawer shows `session.title` directly.
